title: Salman Khan Calls Maatrubhumi Rewrite Claims 'Nonsense' at Trailer Launch
excerpt: The Hindi war drama, earlier titled Battle of Galwan, is 'a film on soldiers and their families on both sides,' the actor said — not an anti-China film, and not rewritten under government pressure.
body:
• Salman Khan dismissed reports that Maatrubhumi is an anti-China film or that the government pressured the makers to rewrite its script, calling the narrative 'nonsense' at the film's trailer launch in Mumbai on Friday.
  • The Hindi film, directed by Apoorva Lakhia and co-starring Chitrangada Singh, is based on the June 15, 2020 Galwan Valley clash and was earlier titled Battle of Galwan.
  • Salman Khan Films has also said the film has not yet been submitted to the CBFC, making reports of certification objections baseless.
  • Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace is scheduled to release in cinemas on December 4; viewers above 75 can watch it for Rs. 11, the actor announced.

Salman Khan has quashed rumours that the Government of India pressured him to change the script of his upcoming war drama Maatrubhumi, or that the film takes a stance against China. Speaking to media at the film's trailer launch in Andheri West, Mumbai, on Friday, he called the narrative nonsense, according to IANS reporting.

"This narrative that we are going against China, and our government has put pressure on us to change its script, and rewrite it — all this is nonsense. It's not true at all. We have made a film on soldiers, their families, and what they go through, what the soldiers from both sides go through. So, there are no negative forces in this."

— Salman Khan, at the Maatrubhumi trailer launch

Khan said the negative element in the film is circumstance, not a side: the soldiers like each other, but when a situation comes, the nation comes first for soldiers on both sides, who then try to solve the issue. Filmfare's account of the launch carried the same clarification, in the actor's mix of Hindi and English.

Title, certification and the earlier version

The film was earlier titled Battle of Galwan and is based on the Galwan Valley stand-off between Indian and Chinese troops on June 15, 2020. Khan explained at the launch that the new title came from a song composed by Himesh Reshammiya, and that the makers had worked on a new version of the film under the director — a creative revision, not an imposed one. Separately, Salman Khan Films has dismissed reports of certification trouble, stating the film has not yet been submitted to the Central Board of Film Certification, so reports of objections or delay are, in the banner's words, false and entirely baseless.

The film and the release

Maatrubhumi: May War Rest in Peace is a Hindi-language war drama directed by Apoorva Lakhia, produced by Salma Khan under Salman Khan Films, and co-stars Chitrangada Singh in a pivotal role. It was originally slated for release in April this year and was later postponed. Bollywood Hungama reported from the launch that the film is now scheduled to release in cinemas on December 4 — and that Khan announced viewers above the age of 75 can watch it for just Rs. 11.
